column1: # deployq target registry.  target <TAB> repo <TAB> wrapper <TAB> probe-url
# The registry is DATA and this file carries the ids, exactly as estate.ids does
# for gcp-actions.sh — so the scripts beside it stay estate-agnostic and can be
# A wrapper must already exist in its repo and be the reviewed deploy path for
# that service. deployq never composes a gcloud command; it runs the wrapper the
# repo already trusts. That is what keeps this from becoming a shell with a JSON
# front door, and it is why gcp-actions.sh can go on refusing to mutate: the
# mutation path is here, named, queued and reported, instead of ad hoc.
# probe-url is what the post-checks interrogate. Leave it "-" if the target
# serves nothing (a job, a migration), and give it no http post-checks.
